summary: Tested the Mayday/Pan-Pan shore contact alert from end to end. Backend: 13/13 pytest tests pass, plus a manual check that accepting with shore_ok:true works (the agreement record was restored afterwards). Covered: raise with and without GPS, idempotency, upgrade, near (<=100 m) and far, stale stand-down -> 409, crew stand-down, a repeated stand-down is idempotent, shore track/boats include the alert, 404 for outsiders and the shore-only user, null alert when the boat has no shore contacts, 422 validation, crew agreement shore_brief and the 400 without shore_ok. Frontend: the skipper's Mayday shows active -> clearing -> cleared -> dismiss. Crew and skipper sync both ways: an alert or stand-down on one phone shows on the other in about 25-30 s. The /shore page works: red notice, pulsing marker, a permanent tooltip, and for far alerts a yellow Last reported marker and a dashed line. The page turns green after stand-down in about 32 s. Near via Playwright geolocation shows 'within 100 m' and only the red marker. Offline (context.set_offline): the alert is queued and sends when the phone comes back online. Agreement dialog: the shore section, the warning when you accept without the tick, and the tick that clears it all work. At 390 px there is no horizontal overflow. Found and FIXED 2 bugs: (1) CRITICAL: cancelling a held offline alert did not remove it from the localStorage queue, so it was still sent to the shore contacts and emailed once signal returned (confirmed in distress_log, alert 33468c27). (2) The ShoreMap alert fitBounds was skipped under React StrictMode's double effect run, so the red marker was off-screen for far alerts. Both fixes were verified in the UI.

minor.issue: The email is sent inline with no retry. During testing the email service returned 429 rate_limited, so emailed=false and that Mayday email was lost for good. The map alert still works. Recommend a retry or background outbox for alert and stand-down emails.
Any different kind replaces the active alert, so a Pan-Pan pressed while a Mayday is active downgrades it to Pan-Pan (upgraded_from=mayDay). Consider never downgrading an active Mayday.
Read-then-write is not atomic. Two phones raising at the same moment can both write and both email. A conditional update would fix this.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent: held.includes(j) compared object references from two separate JSON.parse calls, so nothing was removed. A cancelled alert was still sent when the phone came back online. Now it filters by job id.

FIXED by testing agent: fittedAlert ref was not reset when the map was re-created (StrictMode in dev), so the alert spots were never fitted. The red MAYDAY marker was off-screen when the alert was far from the boat.
hide('cancelled') overwrites mbp_shore_alert_hidden. A cleared alert from the last hour that was already dismissed then reappears as 'Cleared shore contact MAYDAY'.
Before /shore/track loads it renders boat.alert from /shore/boats, which holds only {state, kind}. The notice briefly reads 'MAYDAY pressed / by . No GPS fix when pressed and no earlier position.'

integration_issues.issue: In manual offline mode navigator.onLine is still true, so raise() sends at once (phase sending -> active) and the bar never shows 'queued'. That is arguably safer, but it differs from the spec. Real loss of signal (context.set_offline) queues correctly.
Crew who accepted before this feature have no shore_ok_at, and the checkbox is disabled once accepted, so they are never asked to confirm the shore alert instructions.

issues: The permanent tooltips ('PAN-PAN pressed here · date' and 'Last reported · date') are cut off at the map edges on mobile. Use more fitBounds padding or direction 'auto'.

shore_alert.raise_alert: alert email is fire-once and inline (up to a 30 s httpx timeout blocks the boat phone's response)

ShoreAlertNotice uses boat.alert, which lacks by_name/pos/last

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all flows work after the 2 fixes; minor issues remain)
